hook.text: Bend a wire, heat it, and watch it snap back to its original shape like magic.

buildup.text: Nitinol — nickel-titanium — remembers its shape through a reversible phase change.

discovery.text: Below a critical temperature, atoms rearrange into martensite — flexible and deformable.

twist.text: Heat it above the transition point and atoms snap back to austenite — the original shape.

climax.text: Heart stents made of nitinol expand inside arteries when warmed by body heat.

punchline.text: This metal forgets bending but remembers its shape.

quiz.question: What triggers shape memory alloys to return to their original shape?
options: A temperature change causing a phase transformation
